text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Iraqi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THAWRA
- President Saddam Hussein stresses importance of developing municipal services.
- Aziz says Kuwait is the only country giving U.S. permission to use its territory for military strikes on Iraq.
- Our air defences in southern sector force hostile planes to flee.
- U.N. Security Council agrees to implement requirements of oil-for-food deal.
- Moscow opposes use of force against Iraq.
- Chirac renews France's concern over Iraq's sovereignty.
- U.N. confirms that calm returns to Sulaimaniya.
- Education minister receives Romanian ambassador.
- Italy says Iraq has the right to defend itself.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ)
- Iraq resumes supplying Kurdish areas with fuel.
- Editorial hits out at U.S. President Bill Clinton and Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole.
- Commentary says the United States lost its anti-Iraq card with the return of Iraqi Kurdistan to Baghdad camp.
AL-IRAQ
- Aziz tells CNN that he did not threaten Kuwait. "We wanted the Kuwaiti people get acquainted with the aggressive decision of their rulers," he told the Cable News Network.
- Editorial slams Clinton and Dole for their anti-Iraq policies.
- Iraq's cabinet hails Nigeria's supportive stand toward Iraq.
- Information minister visits press centre, meets foreign reporters.
- Iraq completes preparations for Babylon international festival due on September 22.
